Every S_t(x) has sign x for real 0<|x|<=1. A,B<0 make all terms of p_m'(epsilon_m)-1 negative for epsilon_m=(-1)^(m+1), while C,D>0 make q_m'(x) nonzero for every real x!=0. The sole A^m term exceeds magnitude one for every m>=3 by the rational m=3 certificate (27/25)^3(2+(10/11)^3)/(1+(10/11)^3)^2=1+136271021/1048140625 and strict monotonicity thereafter. Thus p_m' has an interior nonzero real root and the harmonic Jacobian is negative there, while it is +1 at 0, giving an interior Jacobian zero by continuity and nonunivalence by Lewy. Exact rational checker at real bundled path independently verifies critical identities/representative finite m; enumeration is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source resolves the twofold Dorff question, but failure of local univalence under a nonlinear coefficientwise convolution does not automatically persist under repeated application. The all-m>=3 theorem demonstrates a natural infinite-order structural obstruction and identifies the alternating real-axis sign of the analytic critical witness. A single universal exact-sign/magnitude argument covers all higher powers, not a finite census, parameter substitution or arbitrary slice. It addresses the natural continuation of a 2026 counterexample without claiming generality for all convex maps.
